Candidates node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb, node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098, node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913, node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1, node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba, and node.c8bd87cfd64bba8762d9b3a0 omit the source's explicit categories when describing licensed firms.

Candidate node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2 explicitly enumerates the source categories, but treats their assessment as an externally supplied classification rather than implementing the definition. The candidate bindings assign this definition claim to unrelated submission or resubmission controls.
claim.bfdb82e761c518748bcef354 is an authentic descriptive scope statement, but is misassigned to four event-level resubmission controls; the operative trigger comes from da12aecad4e68.u28.3334.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes filings before 9:00am on 2 February 2026, while the source places operational launch at 9:00am and retains blackout urgent-contact arrangements until then; the calendar-date interpretation is not established for the resubmission trigger.

node.f75383097facdc52b0ac66f7 has an unresolved control binding: schema conformity has source support, but adds a condition beyond the selected channel, method and e-Cert control and does not implement the separate requirement to liaise promptly to arrange a technical test.
The definition checks establish retention of the actor category only; they do not establish the correctness of externally supplied licensing classifications or overall compliance.

The source establishes an e-Cert requirement for XML and prescribed PDF submissions but does not establish its operational manner; node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 must not treat an unsupported certificate-use procedure as a source requirement.
The candidates operationalize specific submission-compliance or resubmission questions; none represents the broader descriptive transition claim as such.

claim.965373493eb9af80a62aee31 is supported descriptive background, but is misassigned to all seven executable controls: platform identity and replacement are neither submission compliance nor an event-level resubmission trigger.
The claim's uncertainty statement that footnote 1 is not supplied is stale: da12aecad4e68.u23.2943 supplies its text; the linked presentation itself is not supplied.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 extends its trigger to the hours before the 9:00am launch on 2 February 2026, although da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 says 'following its implementation' and da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 specifies the launch time; the calendar-date interpretation is not established for that interval.

node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2 permits a compliant result based on submission-specific certificate availability, but da12aecad4e68.u30.3569 does not establish that availability satisfies the e-Cert requirement; the prose reservation does not condition the executable result.
The certificate-satisfaction predicates in the other compliance candidates depend on externally established operational requirements; the supplied source does not specify those mechanics.
The separate blackout-contact, report-history, resubmission-performance and XML-transition controls should not be treated as omitted requirements of these narrower typed outputs.
Both claims contain stale missing-footnote assertions: footnote 1 is supplied in u23–u26, and footnote 2 is supplied in u27–u28.
The replacement-description claim is misassigned to node.f75383097facdc52b0ac66f7 and node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3: neither typed output decides platform identity or replacement.
The exclusivity claim is misassigned to the four resubmission.event candidates; their outputs decide a historical duty trigger, not channel compliance or performance of resubmission.
Footnote 2 requires resubmission after an off-channel submission; it does not establish permission to use another channel or negate the original channel requirement.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes events before 9:00am on launch day; treating those blackout events as occurring following implementation is not established by the calendar-date exclusivity wording.

node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2 treats submission-specific certificate availability as sufficient, but footnote 3 does not establish that sufficiency; the prose assumption does not implement a dependency check.
